benedictine-bottoms-wildlife-area.name: Benedictine Bottoms Wildlife Area
sections: Area rules

From October 1 Through March 31 an access/hunting permit is required. These permit are by computer draw only. Applications period will start in July and will be accepted online only at the Special Hunts page.
Off road vehicle, ATV and horse use is prohibited.
No alcohol or cereal malt beverages of any kind are allowed on the area.
Non-toxic shot required for all shotgun hunting
No Turkey hunting permits are being issued at the time for the Benedictine Bottoms.
Rules on all KDWP public lands
Baiting while hunting or preparing to hunt is illegal on public lands (K.A.R. 115-8-23).
Trail or game cameras are prohibited on KDWP public lands and Walk-In Hunting Access (K.A.R. 115-8-25).

No more than two portable blinds or stands per hunter. Stands and blinds must be marked with the owner's name and address or KDWP number. Portable blinds and decoys may not be left unattended overnight.

Stands may not be placed more than 14 days before the season and must be removed within 14 days after it closes; ladders/steps go with the stand. Natural blinds must use on-site herbaceous material or woody debris. Any unoccupied stand may be used by anyone.
Camping only in designated areas where allowed, up to 7 consecutive days; first-come, first-served.
Target shooting only in designated areas. Commercial guiding is prohibited on KDWP lands.
verdict: From fall into late winter, access/hunting here is by KDWP Special Hunts drawing only (see area rules for dates).

cheyenne-bottoms-wildlife-area.name: Cheyenne Bottoms Wildlife Area
sections: Area rules
Vehicles are permitted only on established roads and parking areas. Driving off roads or on roads closed by sign or barrier is prohibited.
Camping is permitted only in the primitive campground located 1/2 mile west of the area office.

The use of watercraft is restricted to minimize disturbance to the wildlife and to ensure a more aesthetically pleasing experience for all visitors. Watercraft are not permitted in the refuge areas. During the waterfowl season, in-water propeller-driven boats and hand powered boats can be utilized in Pools 2, 3 and 4. Airboats are not allowed at any time.
Littering is prohibited. Take all trash with you.

The Mitigation Marsh, located in the southeast portion of the Wildlife Area, is managed as a youth hunting area. It is open to hunters less than 16 years old hunters accompanied by no more than two adults.
Non-toxic shot is required for all shotgun hunting. The possession of lead shot in the field is prohibited.
No shooting is allowed on or from the dikes.

No holes or pits may be dug for any purpose. Portable blinds and temporary blinds made of native vegetation may be used but must be removed within 10 days after the close of the hunting season or after the last day of use.
Prior to hunting any species on Cheyenne Bottoms Wildlife Area, all hunters are required to check-in here, ksoutdoors.com/checkin using your licensing login credentials.
Pools 1, 5 and a portion of Pool 2 are refuge areas and closed to all activities. Exceptions to this occur for some special hunts. Check with wildlife area personnel for more information.
A handicapped accessible hunting/photo blind is available by reservation. Call the office for additional information and reservations.
In the event of whooping crane activity, the pool the birds are in is closed to all hunting and the goose hunting zones are closed to crane and light goose hunting.
Motorized boats are allowed only during an open waterfowl season. All boats must be operated at no wake speeds. Pool 3A is closed to motorized boats. Pool 4A is closed to motorized boats at 1 p.m.

Trapping is permitted on the wildlife area. A special permit is required. It is available at the area office free of charge. However, trapping is not permitted at any time in the refuge area nor during the waterfowl season.
